Selected Work

CAC — Calculated Accurate Clarity

Model accuracy & trust

Rebuilding trust in an AI prediction experts had stopped believing — by closing the loop between production data, user behaviour, and the model.

Clarity correctness16% → 87%
ScopeIndia & Israel
RoleInitiative lead
Context

The platform predicts the clarity grade of a polished stone from a scan of the rough — a prediction planners depend on to decide how to cut. When it's wrong often enough, planners stop trusting the automation and fall back to manual judgment, undermining the product's core value.

Problem

Predicted clarity was correct only ~16% of the time. The hard part: “correctness” had to be defined, measured against real production outcomes, and validated by the planners who make the calls.

My role & process

I led the initiative across India and Israel — driving production-data collection, planner validation sessions, and customer-feedback analysis, then translating planner behaviour into concrete requirements for engineering.

Outcome & learning

Clarity correctness rose to 87%, restoring planner trust. The lesson: model accuracy is a product problem, not just a data-science one — the validation loop mattered as much as the algorithm.

Package Solution Picker

Combinatorial optimization

A decision-support tool that scores and ranks every possible cutting plan across an entire package — turning hours of manual evaluation into seconds.

Combinations27,000+
Planning time~95% faster
Stones / pkgup to 1,900
ApprovalGlobal CEO
Context

A single package can hold up to ~1,900 stones, each with many cutting solutions trading off yield, value, clarity mix, and size. Planners evaluated this by hand, stone by stone.

Problem

No way to make package-level decisions quickly or consistently — and the “best” answer shifts by customer and market, so priority had to be adjustable.

What I built

A browser tool scoring 27,000+ combinations per package: independent yield/value weights, 23 hard filters, a default-vs-optimised view, and manual override with undo.

Outcome & learning

Planning time fell ~95% for the largest packages, with Global CEO approval for customer deployment. The principle: optimize hard, but leave the expert the final, reversible call.

MVP MultiPlan

Configurable planning logic

Designing planning logic flexible enough to encode each customer's priorities — shape, clarity, weight, and inclusion strategy — into one configurable system.

StatusIn progress
MethodResearch-led
RoleInitiative lead
Context

MultiPlan plans several polished stones out of a single rough. But customers optimize for different things — weight retention, specific shapes, clarity outcomes.

Problem

One fixed logic can't serve customers with conflicting priorities. It has to be configurable — without becoming too complex for planners to trust.

My role & approach

I'm leading it end to end: customer research across major clients, and designing configurable logic for shape, clarity, weight, and inclusion strategies — finding the smallest set of controls that flex per customer.

Where it stands

In development. The focus is a configuration model that's expressive enough for real differences, simple enough that planners adopt it.
